entries.name: CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S
entries.notes: The --timeout option takes priority over the variable. When --timeout is not given, a value that does not match the format, or that is zero, makes the script exit with an argparse error (status 2). The empty text is also rejected. When --timeout is given, the variable is not checked at all: argparse converts a text default only for an option that is absent from the command line. bin/slice imports remove_fuse_root from this file (bin/slice:55) and does not use the variable. No file in this area sets it. Count for the checker: the literal name is on 1 lines of the 63 files of this area (0 of them in the two test directories).

readers.mechanism: os.environ.get as the argparse default of --timeout

entries.values: A positive number with an optional unit letter: s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours) or d (days). No letter means seconds. Examples: 10s, 0.1s, 2m.

entries.default: Unset: 10s (10 seconds). An empty value is not treated as unset. It fails the duration check. A --timeout argument to the wrapper replaces the variable.
entries.effect: Time limit for each external command of the FUSE cleanup: each unmount command (fusermount -uz) and the final 'rm -rf --one-file-system'. When a command runs longer, the program sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to its process group and the cleanup fails.
entries.name: CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S
entries.notes: ci-cleanup-fuse-mount.sh does not name the variable. The whole wrapper is 'exec python3 fuse_cleanup.py "$@"', so the read on bin/fuse_cleanup.py line 282 acts on every run of the wrapper. No workflow and no other file of the checkout sets it. bin/slice imports remove_fuse_root from the same file and does not use this read. A bad value stops the program while argparse parses the arguments, before the program looks at the root, unless --timeout is given. This follows from Python's argparse and was not run here.

readers.mechanism: os.environ.get, used as the argparse default of --timeout, in a Python program that the shell wrapper starts with exec and the caller's environment

entries.values: A positive duration. The whole text must be digits, an optional fraction, and an optional unit s, m, h or d. No unit means seconds. Examples: 10s, 0.1s, 2m. Zero, empty text or any other text makes argparse stop with 'expected a positive finite duration, e.g. 10s or 0.1s'.
